content_units: Budget-Friendly Dinner Lineup for Four

Here are   5 dinner options   that fit:   pescatarian  ,   peanut-free  ,   one lactose-intolerant diner  ,   under $60 total grocery budget  ,   under 50 minutes each  , and workable with   just a stovetop + oven  .
Five Dinner Options
Option 1:   Lemon Garlic Baked Salmon, Potatoes, and Green Beans     Sheet-pan style dinner with simple seasoning and minimal cleanup     Approx. $18–$22 total
- Why it fits: Salmon is pescatarian, naturally peanut-free, and dairy-free if you use olive oil instead of butter.
- Time:   40–45 minutes
- Budget note: Works best with frozen or sale-priced salmon fillets.
- Core ingredients: Salmon, potatoes, green beans, lemon, garlic, olive oil.
Option 2:   Tomato Chickpea Pasta with Spinach     Fast pantry dinner that is filling and very low-cost     Approx. $10–$14 total
- Why it fits: Fully pescatarian, peanut-free, and easy to keep lactose-free by skipping cheese or using a dairy-free topping.
- Time:   25–30 minutes
- Budget note: One of the cheapest options here and still substantial for four adults.
- Core ingredients: Pasta, canned chickpeas, canned tomatoes or jarred sauce, spinach, onion, garlic.
Option 3:   Black Bean and Fish Tacos with Cabbage Slaw     Flexible taco dinner with good protein and fresh crunch     Approx. $14–$19 total
- Why it fits: Use white fish plus black beans for a pescatarian meal; keep it peanut-free and lactose-free by using avocado, salsa, and lime instead of cheese or sour cream.
- Time:   30–35 minutes
- Budget note: Tilapia or pollock keeps cost down.
- Core ingredients: Corn tortillas, white fish, black beans, cabbage, lime, salsa, avocado.
Option 4:   Vegetable Fried Rice with Scrambled Eggs and Edamame     One-pan style stovetop meal using affordable staples     Approx. $12–$16 total
- Why it fits: Pescatarian-friendly, peanut-free, and naturally lactose-free.
- Time:   30–40 minutes
- Budget note: Great for using leftover rice or inexpensive frozen vegetables.
- Core ingredients: Rice, eggs, edamame, carrots, peas, onion, soy sauce, sesame oil.
Option 5:   Baked Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Tuna, White Beans, and Herby Salad     Hearty, high-protein dinner with low ingredient cost     Approx. $11–$15 total
- Why it fits: Tuna and beans make it filling, it is peanut-free, and it stays lactose-free without cheese or yogurt toppings.
- Time:   40–50 minutes
- Budget note: Very cost-effective and easy to scale.
- Core ingredients: Sweet potatoes, canned tuna, white beans, lemon, parsley or green onion, salad greens.
Best Fit by Priority
-   Lowest cost:   Tomato Chickpea Pasta with Spinach
-   Best balance of price + protein:   Black Bean and Fish Tacos
-   Most filling on a tight budget:   Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Tuna and White Beans
-   Simplest cleanup:   Lemon Garlic Baked Salmon Tray
-   Fastest pantry-friendly option:   Vegetable Fried Rice with Eggs and Edamame
Shopping Context

Using typical budget grocery pricing, these five dinners are each realistic as   standalone meals under the $60 meal budget cap  , with most landing around   $10–$22 total for four  . The salmon dinner is the priciest, so the others are better if you want maximum savings.
